messages:
Sam: FYI — ran into a weird ESM/CJS + typing combo in the edge sample app. import of @redwood/sdk yields runtime 'Unexpected token "export"' on Cloudflare workers and TS inference collapses overloads to `any`. Anyone seen this?
Aziza: oof. is the sample using `module: commonjs` in tsconfig or a mix in package.json `exports`/`module` fields?
Sam: sample is the tiny worker starter in repo: package.json has "type": "module" and we ship both cjs/esm builds. tsconfig is `module: ESNext`, `moduleResolution: node` — but the compiled bundle still throws.
Jon: can you paste the exact import? Is it `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` or `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`? Edge bundlers sometimes pick the wrong entry.
Sam: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`
Maria: edge runtimes (Cloudflare, Vercel Edge) choke on cjs artifacts. bundlers like esbuild/rollup might prefer `exports['.']` -> conditional exports. if package.json has a `require` main that points to cjs, some bundlers pick it.
Sam: here's the stack: 
```
Error: Unexpected token 'export'
 at file:///var/task/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js:1
```
and TS shows `createClient` type as `any` even though we declare overloads in `index.d.ts`.
Aziza: that sounds like consumers are resolving to the ESM file at runtime but TS is resolving to the CJS types or vice-versa. Could be a types entry mispointing. Do we have `types`/`typings` field in package.json?
Sam: package.json has `types: dist/index.d.ts`, but the dist build emits `dist/esm/index.js`, `dist/cjs/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts`. Not sure if the declaration file maps per-subpath.
Jon: quick workaround: in the edge sample's bundler config (esbuild for worker) force `conditions: ['worker', 'import']` or alias `@redwood/sdk` -> `@redwood/sdk/dist/esm` to ensure ESM runtime + matching d.ts.
Maria: long-term fix: publish per-conditional `exports` with `import`/`require` and also `types` via `exports` subpath: e.g., `exports: { '.': { import: './dist/esm/index.js', require: './dist/cjs/index.js', types: './dist/index.d.ts' } }` — but note TS doesn't read `exports.types` yet, so ideally provide `types` at package root and match layout.
Aziza: also the typing collapse to `any` likely comes from complex overloads + `declarationMap`/composite issues. If tsserver picks up different file than build, overloads can merge oddly. Can you repro locally with `tsserver` watch?
Sam: yep repro with `npx tsc -v` and inside editor. I made a tiny repro that toggles `moduleResolution`/`module` and shows `unknown vs any` leak on generics.
Jon: please post the repro link and minimal steps. we can add a CI check in the SDK repo to run the edge sample build.
Sam: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-repros/edge-interop-175987 — includes two branches: `bad-tsconfig` and `fixed-exports`. steps in README.
BuildBot: CI check failed for branch bad-tsconfig (esbuild bundle error). See: https://ci.internal.redwood/2829
Maria: thanks — I skimmed the repro. quick hack that fixed local build for me: in the SDK package, add explicit `module` field in package.json to `esnext` and in tsconfig set `target: es2020` and `module: es2020` so bundler doesn't mix. but that might break older node consumers.
Aziza: maybe better: set the published `exports` to point `import` -> `./dist/esm/index.mjs`, `require` -> `./dist/cjs/index.cjs`, and keep `types: dist/index.d.ts`. then add a small `types` re-export file at `dist/esm/index.d.ts` that references the root d.ts so TS resolves correctly for subpath imports.
Sam: tried a branch with explicit `.mjs`/`.cjs` outputs and added `exports` mapping — it fixed the runtime error on Cloudflare in the sample. TS still had a generic overload narrowing to `any` in one edge case (overload chain + `unknown` parameter).
Jon: the `unknown` vs `any` situation is usually a typing-design issue. If SDK exports overloads that accept `any` in one overload and `T extends unknown` in another, TS widens to `any`. Might need to prefer `unknown` and avoid `any` in public overloads, or add a narrower generic signature first.
Maria: agreed. also add tests that instantiate the overloads in `tests/ts-compat` using `tsc --noEmit` across a matrix of tsconfigs (esnext/module commonjs, moduleResolution=node, bundler-mode) to catch regressions.
Aziza: next steps: 1) Sam to open PR in sdk repo with export map + .mjs/.cjs outputs (link pls), 2) Jon to add CI tsc compat job, 3) Maria to add docs note for edge sample on bundler aliases, 4) Aziza to follow up on typing fix patch.
Sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1247 — includes changes and a short CHANGELOG entry. CI currently flaky on windows matrix.
Jon: I'll add the tsc compat job and wire to PR as a required check.
Maria: I can add a short note to the edge sample README and include the `alias` snippet: 
```js
// esbuild config snippet
alias: { '@redwood/sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, '../node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm') }
```
Aziza: moving typing follow-up to me. I'll reproduce the overload collapse and propose a signature reorder or split. assigning to @Aziza. :white_check_mark:
Sam: awesome, thanks all. marking this thread resolved for now — will post update when PR merges. :shipit:
